cases.note: GNU 9.7 refuses a separator longer than one byte rather than taking its first byte.
GNU 9.7 reports an explicitly empty --separator instead of falling back to newline.

GNU 9.7 reads the two-character spelling \0 as a NUL separator; each record keeps its terminator, so 3 NUL-terminated records at 2 per file are 4 bytes then 2. The default newline separator would see one 6-byte record.

cases.command: mkdir -p /data/fcC_st && (cd /data/fcC_st && printf 'a0b0c0' > z && split -t 0 -l 2 z d && printf 'a\\b\\c\\' > s && split -t '\' -l 2 s b && cat daa; echo '|'; cat dab; echo '|'; cat baa; echo '|'; cat bab; echo); rm -r /data/fcC_st
for v in abc '\n' '\t' é; do split -t "$v" /data/a.txt /data/fcC_t 2>&1; echo rc=$?; done

expect.stdout:
split: multi-character separator 'abc'
rc=1
split: multi-character separator '\\n'
rc=1
split: multi-character separator '\\t'
rc=1
split: multi-character separator '\303\251'
rc=1
